newsitem.title: USA: Florida Citrus Comm. sees little freeze impact.
newsitem.headline: Florida Citrus Comm. sees little freeze impact.

text.p: The Florida Citrus Commission said Wednesday that state Department of Agriculture inspectors had found only isolated damage at packing houses across Florida as a result of last weekend's freeze, and predicted the impact on growers would be minimal.

After a meeting Wednesday, commission members said they had considered options for dealing with the crop damage, which would have included a complete embargo, in which no fruit would have been shipped out of the state, but decided the situation was nowhere near bad enough for such a drastic measure.

Michael Sparks, deputy executive director of the Florida Citrus Commission, said the commission had ordered increased inspections of oranges and grapefruit to stop any damaged fruit from leaving the state. He said the inspections would take place around the clock over a period of 10 days.
Sparks said the commission expected to have preliminary reports on the extent of the freeze damage in 10 to 15 days, but he expected the effect on growers would be minimal.
"This was going to be the largest crop ever. We were expecting 220 million crates of oranges, and 60 million crates of grapefruit," he said.
